question.problem: Let ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14252505/assets/d1c4fec87897f58b7170a09723fcd2b7f6a2ddcc9ce9a2f52299b7a0580cd922.svg) and ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14252505/assets/ca0a8bd7bfa1ac9750efd56df7960839f64f0414fb086f0c9b24bbd1f3a377ce.svg) Find a unit vector that is parallel to $\mathbf{a}+2\mathbf{b}.$
question.worked_solution:
Remember that to find a unit vector that is parallel to a given vector, we need to divide the given vector by its length:

$$
\begin{aligned}u & =\frac{a+2b}{|a+2b|}\end{aligned}
$$

First, let's compute the sum:

$$
\begin{aligned}a+2b & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+2\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2+2 \\ 0+(-2)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula for the magnitude of a vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}|a+2b| & =\sqrt{{0}^{2}+(-2)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we divide $\mathbf{a}+2\mathbf{b}$ by its length and get the following unit vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}u & =\frac{a+2b}{|a+2b|} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(a+2b) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
